propositions: Bridge orchestration logic must be extracted into a runner-neutral packaged Python core exposing three public interfaces: Python library (rebar.bridge_run), CLI (rebar bridge run --profile), and MCP (write-gated bridge_run tool) that work across all install shapes (pip wheel, Homebrew wheel-backed, MCP Registry/uvx).

Five execution profiles (reconcile-check, dry-run, bootstrap-strict, bootstrap-throttle, live) must map to their corresponding rebar subcommands while preserving provider MODE environment variable compatibility and legacy reconcile result translation (benign results 3/4/75 map to canonical 0 for new runner, direct legacy callers retain original results).

Provider wrappers (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab) must invoke the installed CLI entrypoint exactly as `rebar bridge run` with schema-validated configuration, embedded shell linting via pinned ShellCheck, and immutable GitLab schema provenance validation, eliminating repository-local runner scripts.

The runner must validate shallow repository detection, enforce strict ticket-store delivery with run id and bot identity, respect valid pause markers, and handle malformed markers without silent failure, returning structured output and exit code 1 on delivery failure.

Explicit repo_root parameter must override inherited REBAR_ROOT; installed CLI usage outside a repository must honor configured REBAR_ROOT, and environment validation plus 3600-second timeout enforcement belongs in the Python core.
